proposals.before: His great-grandfather Si had served as magistrate of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture under the Tang, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Si had served as county defender of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture under the Tang, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 縣尉 is the county defender/commandant, not the county magistrate (令); the idiomatic rendering conflates the two offices.

proposals.before: At that time Kong Qian controlled the finances and was intent on squeezing revenue; he repeatedly sent orders to Bian requiring the people to be levied for silk deliveries. Zhi argued vigorously against this, and although his protest was not heeded, public opinion praised him.
proposals.after: At that time Kong Qian controlled the finances and was intent on squeezing revenue; he repeatedly sent orders to Bian requiring the people to be levied for silk deliveries. Zhi argued vigorously against this, and although the measure was not carried out, public opinion praised him.
proposals.reason: 事雖不行 means the levy itself was not put into effect, not that Zhi's protest went unheeded; the current idiomatic reverses the outcome.

proposals.before: Soon he was made Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
proposals.after: Soon he was made Supervising Secretary; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is the Supervising Secretary of the menxia, not a censorial post; Supervising Censor misidentifies the office.

proposals.before: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Censor; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was changed to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
proposals.after: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Secretary; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was changed to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 給事中 should be Supervising Secretary, not Supervising Censor.

proposals.before: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.after: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.reason: 衛尉少卿 is the vice director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia/Guards, not the ancestral temple; 鴻臚卿 is the Court of State Ceremonial, not Imperial Entertainments (光祿).

proposals.before: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; he was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.after: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia; he was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
proposals.reason: 衛尉少卿 and 鴻臚卿 are mistranslated as ancestral-temple and entertainments offices.

proposals.before: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was his colleague but ranked above him in court order. He told Song of his dream and said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position above you!"
proposals.after: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was his colleague, but Zhuanmei ranked above him in court order. He told Song of his dream and said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position above you!"
proposals.reason: Chinese 學士李崧同列而班在其上 plus 處吾子之首 shows Zhuanmei's court place was above Li Song, not the reverse.

proposals.before: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was of the same rank but stood above him in court order; he therefore told Song of his dream and moreover said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position and stand above you!"
proposals.after: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was of the same rank, but Zhuanmei stood above him in court order; he therefore told Song of his dream and moreover said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position and stand above you!"
proposals.reason: 班在其上 refers to Zhuanmei's place above Li Song, matching 處吾子之首; the packet English makes Song the senior.

proposals.before: His grandfather Zhuo had been prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
proposals.after: His grandfather Zhu had been prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
proposals.reason: The given name is 銖 (Zhu), not 棁/涿 (Zhuo); rendering it Zhuo conflates three different Cui men.

proposals.before: His grandfather Zhuo was prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
proposals.after: His grandfather Zhu was prefect of An and Pu prefectures.
proposals.reason: Source 祖銖 is Zhu, not Zhuo.

proposals.before: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to outer director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.
proposals.after: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to vice director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.
proposals.reason: 員外郎 is the vice-director / supernumerary director grade, not an 'outer director'.

proposals.before: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to outer director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.
proposals.after: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was promoted to vice director and controller of edicts, then transferred to secretariat drafter.
proposals.reason: 員外郎 should not be calqued as 'outer director'.

proposals.before: He first served on the staff of Li Cunzhang, military governor of Yun Prefecture; after Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he held aide posts in Yan and Xu in succession.
proposals.after: He first served on the staff of Li Cunzhang, military governor of Yunzhou; after Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he held aide posts in Yun and Xu in succession.
proposals.reason: Chinese 雲州 is Yunzhou, not Yun Prefecture (鄆州); 鄆、徐 are Yun and Xu, so English Yan mistranslates 鄆.

proposals.before: In his youth Guozhen lived through the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji. He tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, then lived as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River, where the brothers Gao Wanxing, all lovers of literature, recruited him as an aide.
proposals.after: In his youth Guozhen lived through the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji. He tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, then lived as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River, where Gao Wanxing and his brothers, all lovers of literature, recruited him as an aide.
proposals.reason: 高萬興兄弟 means Gao Wanxing and his brothers, not a plural 'brothers Gao Wanxing'.

proposals.before: His grandfather Zhao served as Right Majordomo-General of the Martial Guard under Tang.
proposals.after: His grandfather Zheng served as Right Militant Guard Grand General under Tang.
proposals.reason: 晸 is Zheng, not Zhao; 右武衛大將軍 is Militant Guard Grand General, not Majordomo-General.

proposals.before: His grandfather Zhao was Right Majordomo-General of the Martial Guard of Tang.
proposals.after: His grandfather Zheng was Right Militant Guard Grand General of Tang.
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic line: 晸 romanized as Zhao and 大將軍 rendered as Majordomo-General.

proposals.before: His father Cunjing was military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong under Liang and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Central Secretariat Director; the Liang History contains his biography.
proposals.after: His father Cunjing was acting military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong under Liang and was posthumously granted successive honors culminating in Central Secretariat Director; the Liang History contains his biography.
proposals.reason: 梁河中節度觀察留後 is an acting residual post (留後), not full military governor; 累贈 is posthumous grant, not ennoblement.

proposals.before: During Qingtai he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Receptions.
proposals.after: During Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Palace Administration.
proposals.reason: 殿中監 is the Director of the Palace Administration, not Supervisor of the Palace Receptions.

proposals.before: During Qingtai he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Receptions.
proposals.after: During Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Palace Administration.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 殿中監 as Palace Receptions.

proposals.before: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Jiju, was the nephew by marriage of Tang chancellor Duke of Qi, Guangfeng.
proposals.after: Zhao Xi, courtesy name Jiju, was the brother's son of Tang chancellor Duke of Qi, Guangfeng.
proposals.reason: 猶子 is an agnatic nephew (brother's son), not a nephew by marriage.

proposals.before: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Yan recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army, and he served in succession as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
proposals.after: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Xun recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army, and he served in succession as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
proposals.reason: 劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩, Xún), not Yan.

proposals.before: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Yan recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army; he successively served as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
proposals.after: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Xun recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army; he successively served as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
proposals.reason: 劉鄩 is Liu Xun (鄩, Xún), not Yan.

proposals.reason: 劉鄩 is Liu Xun, not Liu Yan.

proposals.before: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yin, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
proposals.after: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
proposals.reason: 羅隱之 is Luo Yinzhi, not the Tang poet Luo Yin.

proposals.before: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yin; people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
proposals.after: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi; people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
proposals.reason: 羅隱之 is Luo Yinzhi, not Luo Yin.

proposals.before: He spent his days with Luo Yin, who made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from hillside fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry well, and were skilled at long whistling.
proposals.after: He spent his days with Luo Yinzhi, who made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from hillside fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry well, and were skilled at long whistling.
proposals.reason: 羅隱之 should be Luo Yinzhi throughout.

proposals.before: He spent his days and nights in company with Luo Yin; Yin made a living through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself with hillside fields. Both loved wine and were skilled at poetry, and excelled at long whistling.
proposals.after: He spent his days and nights in company with Luo Yinzhi; Yinzhi made a living through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself with hillside fields. Both loved wine and were skilled at poetry, and excelled at long whistling.
proposals.reason: 隱之 is Yinzhi, not Yin.

proposals.before: Luo said, "When drunk, apart from Yin and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
proposals.after: Luo said, "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
proposals.reason: 隱之 here is Luo's own name Yinzhi, not Yin.

proposals.before: Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yin and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
proposals.after: Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
proposals.reason: 隱之 is Yinzhi, not Yin.

proposals.before: Some even came from more than a thousand li beyond Yue and sent painters to sketch his likeness in secret and mount it on screens.
proposals.after: Some even from beyond a thousand li sent painters to sketch his likeness in secret and mount it on screens.
proposals.reason: 越千里之外 means even from beyond a thousand li, not the Yue region.

proposals.before: There were also those from more than a thousand li beyond Yue who sent painters to sketch his likeness secretly and array it on screens.
proposals.after: There were also those from more than a thousand li away who sent painters to sketch his likeness secretly and array it on screens.
proposals.reason: 越 here means to exceed, not the place Yue.
